profile.campus: West Des Moines, Iowa (Polk County portion of Microsoft's multi-campus Azure hub)
profile.address: 215 Pine Avenue, West Des Moines, Polk County, Iowa, 50265
profile.reading: This building is part of Microsoft's West Des Moines, Iowa data center hub, a cluster of campuses the company has built since first opening in the city in 2012. Microsoft has invested an estimated $5 billion to $6 billion across its West Des Moines facilities to date, per reporting from Wisconsin Public Radio, which visited the site while researching a comparable Microsoft project in Wisconsin, and the company now owns more than 600 acres across the metro. West Des Moines' city engineer told WPR that each Microsoft campus typically comprises three to four buildings and takes roughly eight to ten years to fully build out, which is consistent with this registry finding multiple OSM-mapped Microsoft buildings clustered along the same streets in Dallas, Polk, and Warren counties. More than 600 people now work across Microsoft's West Des Moines data centers, in roles spanning mechanical and electrical engineering, campus management, IT operations, security, and building maintenance, making Microsoft roughly the seventh- or eighth-largest full-time employer in a city of about 73,000 residents. One of the named campuses, internally called Project Osmium, sits on the south side of West Des Moines near Interstate 35; the Business Record has separately reported on a sixth Microsoft data center project, called Project Ruthenium, planned near Veterans Parkway and Woodland Avenue with an initial $210 million, 245,000-square-foot building and roughly 25 permanent jobs, part of a site that could eventually hold up to four buildings. This building sits along Pine Avenue, Southeast White Crane Road, or the Military Order of the Purple Heart Highway in Polk County, in the eastern portion of Microsoft's West Des Moines footprint; Microsoft has not published which named campus or project this specific building belongs to, nor its individual square footage or MW capacity, consistent with the company's general practice of not disclosing per-building specifics for its Azure data centers.

reading.body:
Microsoft's West Des Moines campus in Polk County is part of a multi-county investment reported at $1.5–2 billion with a planned sixth data center, but Microsoft does not publish power capacity, square footage, or facility-specific MW figures for individual Azure campuses, disclosing only aggregate worldwide statistics. The campus cannot therefore be quantified against its stated expansion plans or ranked within Iowa's published capacity by this registry's method.

Iowa has 52 mapped data center facilities and only 2 with published power specifications totaling 18 MW, neither of which is this Microsoft campus. This campus ranks third in the state by published megawatts, a ranking that reflects the state context of 52 mapped facilities, not this campus's actual size.

Without published specifications, this campus's relevance to AI scaling cannot be determined from grid capacity or compute density. Its significance rests on reported investment scale, multi-county footprint, and explicit plans for expansion, all non-quantified by power or floor area.
